label: prop:cl3-zeta5-pslq-independence
title: PSLQ certifies Cl$_3$(2$\pi$/5) $-$ Cl$_3$(4$\pi$/5) is independent of standard depth-3 periods up to coefficient norm 10$^8$
html:
PSLQ searches at 70 decimal places with a coefficient norm bound of 10^8 certify that the difference

  X \;:=\; \mathrm{Cl}_3\!\left(\tfrac{2\pi}{5}\right) - \mathrm{Cl}_3\!\left(\tfrac{4\pi}{5}\right)
  \;\approx\; 0.955723\ldots

admits no \mathbb{Q}-linear relation with any standard weight-3 period basis elements.

The test subjects X against candidate bases including \{\zeta(3), \pi^3\} and full golden-ratio logarithmic bases. No relation emerges. While not a proof of irreducibility, the negative PSLQ result provides the strongest unconditional canonical evidence that X constitutes a genuinely independent depth-3 period. The depth-3 surface for \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5) reduces to this single real period.

What is proved is the identification of X: the coefficient \cos(2\pi n/5) - \cos(4\pi n/5) equals \tfrac{\sqrt5}{2}\,\chi_5(n), where \chi_5 is the quadratic character modulo 5, so

  X \;=\; \tfrac{\sqrt5}{2}\, L(3, \chi_5),
  \qquad L(3, \chi_5) \;=\; \sum_{n \geq 1} \frac{\chi_5(n)}{n^3}.

The \mathbb{Q}-linear independence of L(3,\chi_5) from \zeta(3) and \pi^3 is not known; the PSLQ result is evidence for it, not a proof.

Comparison with the standard-relation dimension bound for \mathrm{MPV}(3,5) clarifies the scope of the candidate basis. At weight 3 and prime level N = 5, the 5^2(5+1) = 150 multiple polylogarithm values satisfy Deligne and Goncharov's motivic upper bound d(3,5) \le D(3,5) = (\varphi(5)/2 + 1)^3 = 27, which finite and regularized double-shuffle relations together with lifted weight-1 relations tighten to d(3,5) \le \mathrm{SR}(3,5) = 22 = (5^3 + 4\cdot 5^2 + 5\cdot 5 + 14)/12 [zhao2010-standard-relations, \S\S 7.3--7.4, \S 9 Table 2, Conj. 9.2]. Of the eight periods tested against X = \tfrac{\sqrt{5}}{2} L(3,\chi_5) \in \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{MPV}(3,5), the five level-1 and level-5 terms \{\zeta(3), \pi^3, \pi\log^2\varphi, \log^3\varphi, \pi^2\log\varphi\} span the real level-1 line and decomposable lower-weight products inside \mathrm{MPV}(3,5), while \{\pi\log^2 2, \pi^2\log 2, \log^3 2\} test cross-level independence against level 2; the remaining dimension up to \mathrm{SR}(3,5) = 22 accommodates X alongside imaginary parity components and higher-depth generators L_5(2,1\mid \cdot) and L_5(1^3\mid \cdot).
